text:
This page provides both the trope patterns for the selected portion and optionally displays the Hebrew text as well.  When this window opens only the trope names are displayed for each of tropes attached to text in that line using a transliterated text of the trope name,  such as Munach or Darga.  When a line text box is clicked there is audio feedback of the melody of each trope in the line sequence but there is no attempt at pronunciation of these names.  Rather the melody is played using  sounds as if the notes were being 'hummed.'   When playback is active,  a text box popup appears with the trope names spelled out in Heberw text.  There is a button at the top of the page that is used to set text highlighting during playback.  If checked,  each trope name word is highlighted as is voiced.  A button is also available to provide a 'smooth playback'  which attempts to minimize delays between the succesive word playbacks. When a selected portion name is selected by clicking in the portion name identifier, such as 'Yitro',  the screen disiplays a line of Hebrew lyrics text under each of the trope pattern lines. Additionally,  a musical note symbol appears to the left of the title box and is shaded with a light green background.  To the right of the info symbol following the title field there may be a check box labeled 'Use Pocket Torah.'  This only appears if the selected portion has been coded for Pocket Torah playback which is limited to text completely within a single aliyah based on the full annual K'riyah.   The note symbol and each of the lines of Hebrew lyrics are clickable objects to initiate audio plaback.  If  'Use Pocket Trainer' is checked,  any audio playback will utilized a connection to Pocket Torah.com to retun the lyrics displayed using the trope for that line as recorded on that site.   If unchecked,  the audio is from a saved recording genereted by licensed access to TropeTrainer.com and played source files saved with the application.  Please click on 'License Information' on the main page for more details.

Note that the trope pattern names may not correspond exactly to expected names as this application uses alternative names for certain trope patterns for efficiency, such as for Kadman-V'azlah where two trope marks are reference as a single reference and the two words to which these are attached appear as a single combination word in the text during playback.  It is possible that the application has trope patterns and no lyrics.  If this is the case,  no Hebrew text appears when the name box is clicked.

When not actively in audio mode,  if the Hebrew text is displayed,  hovering over a word will open a tooltip window containing  an enlarged word image under which is the tranliteraion of that word. If using a touch device,  the hover action is triggered by touching and holding one's finger on the target.  The tool tip should disappear when the target is no longer selected by either mechanism. Note that the generic note sequence used for the trope name playback can be viewed from the main trope table by clicking the trope name in the table to open the Trope Info display which includes the musical note notation for each of the tropes using a standard five line music staff. Due to variations in  the mechanism used to generate audio playback,  the actual trope sounds may differ in tonality and pattern i.e.  Trope Trainer or Pocket Torah generated souces,  and these may not conform identically to the note pattern used in the trope pattern playbck.
